title: Пари на пять тысяч рублей  (A Five-Thousand-Ruble Bet)

segments.t: When Chef Barinov tries to ask Elena out in person using an old-fashioned bouquet, his nerves get the better of him and he freezes up. Returning to the kitchen trembling with frustration, Barinov orders Max to bet him five thousand rubles that he cannot ask Elena out on a date.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'May I have a word with you for a minute?' Max prompts openly as the beat lands, anchoring the Russian line on "mozhno" ("may, can") and "minutku" ("a minute") without extra filler.
'I did not quite catch that.' Barinov offers a wry direction straight away, putting "ponyala" ("understood") alongside "ne" ("not") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Go on a date with you?' Elena queries quietly on the spot, leaning on "svidaniye" ("date") before closing the thought with "na" ("on, onto").
'With an old, fat alcoholic?' Max checks honestly as the talk turns, pairing "starym" ("old") with "tolstym" ("fat, thick") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'I just cannot do it.' Barinov shares a resolute style without hesitation, putting "mogu" ("can") alongside "ya" ("I") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Vitya, pull yourself together.' Elena conveys a clear direction as they talk, using "vitya" ("Vitya") by itself, a common way spoken Russian keeps fast dialogue punchy.
'Look at you, you are shaking.' Max establishes a steady stance as they talk, combining "tryaseshsya" ("to tremble") and "da" ("yes") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Be quiet and make a bet with me.' Barinov shows a warm note beside Max, linking "pomolchi" ("to be quiet"), "pospor" ("to make a bet"), and "so" ("with") in one brisk exchange.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
'Bet me that I will not ask Elena out on a date.' Elena strikes a candid tempo with Barinov, linking "priglashu" ("will invite"), "svidaniye" ("date"), and "chto" ("what") in one brisk exchange.
'How much are we betting?' Max prompts promptly in this moment, weaving "sporim" ("wanna bet") together with "na" ("on, onto") just the way native speakers do.
'Five thousand rubles.' Barinov presents an honest tempo with Elena, leaning on "tysyach" ("thousand") before closing the thought with "pyat" ("five").
'Here, take it.' Elena keeps a lively posture with Max, weaving "vozmi" ("take, pick up") together with "da" ("yes") just the way native speakers do.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?

'I bet you do not have the guts to ask Elena out on a date?' Max prompts sharply to Barinov here, linking "sporim" ("wanna bet"), "slabo" ("weakly, dare you"), and "priglasit" ("to invite") in one brisk exchange.
Что я не приглашу Елену на свидание.
Спорим, что вам слабо пригласить Елену на свидание?
That wraps up this scene as after Chef Barinov chickens out of asking Elena on a date in person, he forces Max to bet him five thousand rubles that he cannot get a date with her. See you next time!
